newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline ends steady, buoyed by NYMEX, Med.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline ends steady, buoyed by NYMEX, Med.

text.p: NWE gasoline ended steady on Tuesday, falling early on Monday's crude sell-off and then climbing back to unchanged as Brent crude futures tacked on nearly 60 cents a barrel late today.
Barges were still seen well supplied with greater demand for cargoes, particularly after NYMEX gasoline futures gained more than 2.0 cents a gallon on Tuesday.
"The market is getting more into balanced but there is better cargo demand than barge demand," an ARA trader said.
Eurograde barges ended at $200/$202 fob ARA, basically unchanged. The last trade heard was a 2,000 tonne barge at $201 for first half March delivery.
Regular unleaded also ended unchanged at $195/$197 after earlier trading at $192 and $193, traders said.
U.S. traders expect tonight's American Petroleum Institute report to show a build in gasoline inventories of 0.50 million barrels.
A strong Mediterranean market continued to attract interest for shipping material down from NWE, traders said, but there were still no confirmed, public deals.

In addition, Nigeria, which has been noticeably absent from the Med for the last few months, was expected to step up its products purchases very soon as traders bet that its refineries will not be able to hold out at their higher utilisation rates.
Any demand from Nigeria, which normally buys five to 10 cargoes a month in total of low octane cat gas, may draw more cargoes into the Med from NWE, traders said.
